action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

All Orca behaviour below matches upstream merge base `3ffb9585d2`, checked line by line, unless I mark it "inferred". Paths are relative to `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/filament-step-design-918d1e/`.

## 1. Incompatible filaments in Orca's UI

**There is no `show_incompatible_presets` preference.** The only related setting is `show_unsupported_presets` (default false, `src/libslic3r/AppConfig.cpp:347-348`). It sits in Preferences, Developer tab, as "Show unsupported presets". Its tooltip reads "Show incompatible/unsupported presets in the printer and filament dropdown lists. These presets cannot be selected." (`src/slic3r/GUI/Preferences.cpp:1984`). Changing it refreshes the sidebar filament combos (`Preferences.cpp:1073-1075`).

**The Tab's show/hide toggle is dead code.**
- `m_show_incompatible_presets` starts false, and the `flag_red`/`flag_green` bitmaps load (`src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp:270-272`).
- The button is never created (`Tab.cpp:274`, commented out). Its Bind is commented out (`Tab.cpp:544-546`), and so is the tooltip update (`Tab.cpp:6944-6947`).
- So `TabPresetComboBox::show_incompatible` stays false (`src/slic3r/GUI/PresetComboBoxes.hpp:232`).

**Sidebar filament combo** (`PlaterPresetComboBox::update`):
- Incompatible presets go into `uncompatible_presets` (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:1233-1237`).
- They are listed only when the preference is on, under "Unsupported presets" (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:1429-1430`). Those rows are disabled (`DD_ITEM_STYLE_DISABLED` and `LABEL_ITEM_DISABLED`, `PresetComboBoxes.cpp:1381-1386`), and clicking one does nothing (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:940-948`).
- This also applies to the slot's currently selected preset when it is incompatible. It is never appended, so the combo falls back to item 1 (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:190-191`). That reading is inferred from the code; the comment at `PresetComboBoxes.cpp:1102-1103` says the opposite.
- The red flag is drawn by `get_bmp` (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:660`, `:739`). In practice it only shows in the Tab combo.

**Tab combo:** it hides incompatible presets except the selected one, which shows with the red flag (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:1692`).

**Selection policy:**
- `PresetSelectCompatibleType` has three values: `Never`, `OnlyIfWasCompatible`, `Always` (`src/libslic3r/Preset.hpp:455-462`).
- When the printer or process changes, the filament policy is `OnlyIfWasCompatible` only if the filament Tab's flag is set. Since the flag is always false, the result is `Always` (`Tab.cpp:6196-6204`).
- Under `Always`, every slot whose preset is incompatible is replaced by `first_compatible`. Preference goes to `default_filament_profile` and the same `filament_type` (`src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp:5441-5456`).
- After a save, the policy is `Never`, which keeps red-flagged presets selected (`Tab.cpp:6741`).

**Can a slot keep an incompatible filament?** Through the sidebar UI, no. Selection itself has no guard: `set_filament_preset` simply assigns (`PresetBundle.cpp:5513-5520`), and so does the sidebar path (`src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:9554-9555`). So an incompatible slot survives until the next printer change. It can come from a loaded project, or from JusPrin's `select_filament_preset` used by the agent adapter (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1410`).

**Slicing (inferred):** it does not check preset compatibility. Neither `Print.cpp` nor `PrintApply.cpp` reads `compatible_printers`, and the exported config drops both keys (`PresetBundle.cpp:4113-4114`). I found no warning tied to incompatible presets. The only near-match is the AMS-sync message "There are some unknown or incompatible filaments mapped to generic preset…" (`Plater.cpp:3621`).

## 2. How compatibility is decided (`src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp`)

**`is_compatible_with_printer`** (`Preset.cpp:809-841`), in order:
1. A preset from OrcaFilamentLibrary is rejected if the printer's name or its `inherits()` is in `m_excluded_from` (`:815-823`).
2. If `compatible_printers` is empty and `compatible_printers_condition` is set, the condition decides. A parse error counts as compatible (`:825-835`).
3. Otherwise it is compatible if any of these holds (`:837-840`):
   - it is the default preset;
   - `compatible_printers` is empty (so both empty means compatible with every printer);
   - the list contains `active_printer.preset.name` exactly;
   - or the printer is non-system and the list contains its direct parent `inherits()` (`:799-807`).
- A non-empty list overrides the condition.
- Matching uses the preset name or the parent name only. Aliases are not checked, nor grandparents (FIXME at `:803`).

**`is_compatible_with_print`** follows the same rules with `compatible_prints` (`Preset.cpp:771-791`).

**Inheritance:** a user preset with `inherits` starts from the parent's full config, `compatible_*` included, and applies its saved diff on top (`Preset.cpp:1673-1677`). The diff is all that gets saved (`Preset.cpp:691-724`). User filaments have `vendor == nullptr`, so they are always visible (`Preset.cpp:857`).

**Save-as** (`Tab::save_preset`):
- The dialog title is "Save %s as". It offers "User Preset" or "Preset Inside Project". "Detach from parent" appears only in Developer mode (`src/slic3r/GUI/SavePresetDialog.cpp:56`, `:107-121`).
- When a new filament is saved from a **system** filament whose `compatible_printers` is empty, Orca writes `[selected printer's base]`. The base is the system parent of a user printer (`Tab.cpp:6706-6714`).
- `save_current_preset` does not touch compatibility keys. It sets `inherits` to the old name for a base preset, or clears it when detaching (`Preset.cpp:2926-2932`).
- On load, a root user filament with an empty list gets the part of its name after "@" written into `compatible_printers` (`Preset.cpp:1711-1720`).

**Does a new user printer inheriting "Prusa MK4 0.4 nozzle" see existing user filaments?**
- Yes, if the filament's list contains "Prusa MK4 0.4 nozzle", through the parent rule. This is the usual result of saving from a system filament while on that printer.
- Yes, if both the list and the condition are empty.
- No, if the list names only another user printer, or a different system printer.
- A side effect: saving from a system filament that relied only on a condition pins the copy to one printer.

## 3. Orca's own ways to create a filament

**(a) `CreateFilamentPresetDialog`**, titled "Create Filament":
- Fields: "Vendor" ("Select Vendor", "Can't find vendor I want", "Input Custom Vendor"), "Type", "Serial" ("e.g. Basic, Matte, Silk, Marble"). Then "Filament Preset", with the radios "Create Based on Current Filament" or "Copy Current Filament Preset ". The button is "Create" (`src/slic3r/GUI/CreatePresetsDialog.cpp:658-704`, `:770-949`, `:1044`).
- The base presets offered are root presets only (no `inherits`) of the chosen type. They come from user presets plus visible loaded presets (`CreatePresetsDialog.cpp:1224-1235`, `:1447-1478`).
- The printer checkboxes are visible printer presets, user ones included. A base with an empty list offers all visible printers; otherwise only the listed printers that are visible (`CreatePresetsDialog.cpp:966-998`, `:1481-1489`). So the printer must already be installed.
- Each ticked printer produces "Vendor Type Serial @printer" with `compatible_printers=[printer]` (`CreatePresetsDialog.cpp:1150-1155`, `Preset.cpp:2835-2844`). The result is detached (`inherits` cleared) and saved as a full config (`Preset.cpp:2764`, `:2794`).
- **Entry point:** the "Create New" button on the library page's "Custom Filaments" tab (`resources/web/guide/23/index.html:111`). The chain is `create_custom_filament` → `EVT_CREATE_FILAMENT` → `on_create_filament` (`resources/web/guide/23/23.js:127`, `src/slic3r/GUI/WebGuideDialog.cpp:421-423`, `Plater.cpp:11558-11568`).
- Editing an existing custom filament opens `EditFilamentPresetDialog`. Its "+ Add Preset" button opens a per-printer clone dialog (`CreatePresetsDialog.cpp:4732`, `:4955-4962`).

**(b) Tab "save as"** works as described in section 2.

**(c) "Add/Remove filaments"** is the last sidebar combo item (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:1461`). It runs `run_wizard(SP_FILAMENTS)`, which opens the web `GuideFrame` at `BBL_FILAMENT_ONLY`, `guide/23` (`GUI_App.cpp:8975-8980`, `WebGuideDialog.cpp:241-243`). That page has "System Filaments" and "Custom Filaments" tabs with printer, filament type and vendor filters (`index.html:22-23`, `:35-65`).

There is no "Create filament" item in the combo itself. The printer combo has "Create printer" (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:1466`). The sidebar's "Edit preset" and "Add/Remove presets" menu items exist (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:1065-1093`). `FilamentPickerDialog` is only a colour picker for Bambu filaments (`PresetComboBoxes.cpp:861`).

## 4. JusPrin filament chip menu (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/FilamentMenu.cpp`)

**Views:** a slot list when there are several slots, otherwise the single slot's view (`FilamentMenu.cpp:314-323`). Everything stays in one popup, and the popup closes and reopens around modal dialogs (`:294-304`).

**Slot list** (`FilamentMenu.cpp:350-393`):
- An optional "Use what's loaded on the printer…" row. When the printer is offline it is greyed with "%s is offline. Turn it on to read what's loaded." (`:325-348`).
- A "FILAMENTS ON %s" title (printer caption, e.g. "PRUSA MK4 · 0.4").
- One row per slot: number, colour dot, alias, nozzle, and "on plate" when used.
- "Add a slot".

**Slot view** (`FilamentMenu.cpp:395-483`):
- Title "FILAMENT ON %s", or the back row "FILAMENT · SLOT %d · %s".
- A colour row headed "COLOUR": the current and saved swatches, up to 16 cells, plus a "+" cell whose tooltip is "Other colour…" (`:153`, `:167`, `:485-538`).
- "INSTALLED": the filament list, with a check mark on the slot's current preset.
- "Other filament…" → `open_filament_library()`.
- "Filament settings…" → `ShellController::open_filament_help`. This opens JusPrin's filament help task chat, not the Tab (`ShellController.cpp:1129-1139`).
- "Add a slot", in single-slot mode only.

**Filament list** (`SetupCommands::compatible_filaments`, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:200-220`):
- Only presets that are `is_visible && is_compatible && !is_default`. User presets are included and are not shown separately.
- Sorted by `filament_vendor`, then by alias with the "@…" part removed (`SetupCommands.cpp:32-38`).
- No grouping, no search, no "show incompatible", no "edit", no "create".
- If the current preset is incompatible, nothing in the list is checked (inferred).

**`select_filament_preset`** (`SetupCommands.cpp:310-351`) mirrors the sidebar sequence, including the default colour, flush and tab steps. It does no compatibility check.

**`open_filament_library`** calls `wxGetApp().run_wizard(RR_USER, SP_FILAMENTS)` (`SetupCommands.cpp:557-563`). That is the same page as Orca's "Add/Remove filaments", so "Create New" on it reaches Orca's Create Filament dialog. Its only caller is "Other filament…" (`FilamentMenu.cpp:454`).

**Other SetupCommands:**
- `set_filament_colour` mirrors the combo's colour sync (`SetupCommands.cpp:353-384`).
- `add_filament_slot` calls the sidebar's `add_filament` (`SetupCommands.cpp:386-400`).
- `open_filament_settings` selects the slot's preset in the Tab and opens it (`SetupCommands.cpp:541-555`).
- `sync_from_printer` selects the named printer's device and calls `sync_ams_list` (`SetupCommands.cpp:565-587`).
- The header also lists the printer, bed-type and monitor helpers (`SetupCommands.hpp:142-174`).
